item.title: Re: The Lightswitch
item.content:encoded:
The GOI then used this to its own advantage, killing targets and employees with high levels of skill/competence/important memories and then adding them to some central source (becoming a sort of librarian/bookkeeper of minds).

Honestly not sure why you need to go here… its much more interesting of an anomaly without the edgy "they used it to assassinate people" trope.

So the anomaly is interesting, but I feel your execution is fairly tropey. I'd be much more interested in a narrative about identity than about some mystical bad guy from a GOI.

Moreover, there's very little narrative here. As described it is a short concept that is focused on how the anomaly works, without more substantive storytelling.

I think this is a pretty novel idea, and could be used to tell an interesting story, so I would suggest workshopping some concepts that this anomaly could be used to explore.

item.title: J SCP: The Element of Surprise
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: J SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Joke SCP, Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP page

Elevator Pitch: An incident involving a Scranton Reality Anchor releases a new element into the atmosphere: the Element of Surprise. This element affects the Hume levels on a small area around it, creating unforeseeable results akin to Alchemy (transformation of one element into another, creating life, etc).

Central Narrative: Following the incident researchers notice that their experiments are yielding crazy results. Both super advanced experiments and simple stuff like making grilled cheese present impossible outcomes. The page shows reports of some failed experiments and the comically truncated investigation to understand the phenomenon. Finally they isolate the new element and devise a way to contain it: a multilayered sphere made of random materials that can resist the alterations caused by the Element of Surprise, maintenance includes adding new layers at random intervals to prevent ruptures.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

  • Cartoon-like humor with the failed experiments
  • New element that can be used in future articles and tales

Additional Notes: I don't have a lot of expertise on Joke SCPs but this idea seemed worth investing on. I'm open to all crits and suggestions :)


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: J SCP: The Element of Surprise

I had trouble reading this at first because I don't think the tone behind some of the dialogue was clear to me the first time.

+ Dialogue tone
– hide block

The lines

Rex: Yes. You're like if someone tried making a really shitty Little Mister.

and

Rex: Of course you don't understand. You're just a stupid little plastic failure of a children's product.

…for example, read as stilted to me until I read a second time and imagined Rex as a dude who genuinely doesn't give a shit about Taste, beyond disgust. Imagining him just kinda muttering that second line while loading stuff into the cart really helped it feel more natural. But then lines like

Rex: Indeed! Now, let's begin. It says here you are coated in ethylene glycol?

and

Rex: Do not press this further.

are so formally phrased that it kind of breaks that dispassionate and condescending character. That contrast makes the dialogue feel difficult for me to emotionally follow.

That aside, I enjoy the way you juxtapose the emotional abuse of a sentient being with its similarly unconcerned treatment under Foundation bureaucracy. It gives a sense of how little the Foundation cares about small-fry objects like Taste beyond being a means to some end. Personally I think Taste's abuse isn't particularly more interesting or emotionally engaging on its own than any other article in which a sentient SCP is cruelly treated, even though Taste's childlikeness does make it sting a little. It's those bureaucratic and cold emails that do it for me. I also like the subtle commentary on brand loyalism under capitalism, intentional or not. You'd think a dude mass-producing child-marketed and extremely dangerous anomalies would be given equal concern by the foundation regardless of brand, but.

+ stupidly small nitpick
– hide block

The "to do so" in "It is sentient and capable of speech, despite lacking the necessary organs to do so" should be chopped.

Let me know if I'm reading that dialogue wrong.

item.title: Re: A problem with alot of scp articles.
item.content:encoded:
SCP-914 was written over 12 years ago, making it among the earliest work on the site. The quality of the writing may not be up to current site standards, but it's kept around due to its overwhelming popularity, which is valid even if some of that popularity is based in nostalgia. The original author is rarely on the site anymore, so it's unlikely to see edits to bring it up to current writing standards or tastes.

If you haven't done so, I recommend you read some more recent work, to see how articles may look different these days. Top Rated New Pages, accessible from the side bar menu, is a great place to start. Or, if you like the subjects of the SCPs, but not the article format, try reading some tales instead.

item.title: Re: IMAGINE YOU WERE THERE: Potential SCP
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

Okay, let's see what we have…. Beware. I'm blunt and straight to the point.

A sadistic man tells stories of violence and death. People who listen are entranced. However, as the story goes on, listeners start to show signs of physical trauma. When the man finishes his story, any wounds inflicted on the characters in the story appear on the listener, often killing them.

Okay, so he's a sadistic human that uses mind affecting abilities. I got that. But why? Why does he kill people? Why does he do what he does?

The concept is introduced in the Containment Procedures and Description. The SCP is relatively easy to contain, except that his anomalous abilities increase over time unless he is given a D-class to tell a story to. If he is not sated within 8 days, his anomalous abilities begin to work over video, radio, and recordings. If he cannot tell anyone a story in 15 days, he will begin to project mental images of torture and killing into the minds of people outside his containment. After 21 days, this starts to cause minor but real physical damage to those affected. After 28 days, he mentally projects his image of agony onto everyone within several kilometers, which kills most of those affected.

Okay, so you've talked about how his ability increases every day and it eventually kills people within several kilometers. How long does this last? Does it reset? Does it stay in a several kilometer range until it's finished? Either way, why don't they just lock him up in an cell outside that radius and just use other means to research the subject?

The SCP was discovered and contained after a series of anomalous murders in Tokyo. The SCP seems to understand more about its powers than the Foundation does, and has caused a number of incidents and containment breaches.

It sounds like he's just here to be a headache for the Foundation and nothing more, which brings me to my next thing.

In an interview, the SCP recounts its childhood psychopathy, its path to becoming a serial killer, and how it attained its anomalous abilities.

Care to expand on that? Up to this point you've only explained how much of a danger this guy is and his abilities. You haven't really talked about the narrative in any great detail.

Overall thoughts: Other then the fact that anomalous human affecting people's mind has been done before, this doesn't seem to have any unique concept. Just dangerous to be dangerous. You hinted at a story, but to no detail. Some of the points didn't seem to be needed either, like;

The concept is introduced in the Containment Procedures and Description.

What concept? The narrative? The abilities? I'm not sure what you're referring to.

If you could clear some stuff up, I could look over it again.

- Close

item.title: Re: June the 31st
item.content:encoded:
And…that didn't answer any questions, so putting it more bluntly:

1) This is a Keter-level event as it has the potential to see a lot of dead people, or at least inconvenienced ones. If fishermen are tracking a school of fish, this would put them a day behind, possibly causing them to miss a needed harvest. Unless doctors' idea of a great time is remaining on shift, you are going to see a lot of deaths as simple injuries become much more complicated due to the lack of immediate care; this even would encourage more bravery in individuals so you would see more accidents.

You would also see a lot of pregnancies result in deaths, as well as more mysterious pregnancies.

And if people are truly occupying their lives, expressing themselves fully, keep in mind that this frees all of those with murderous and other ill intents. If my idea of a tranquil day is one where I kill all of my enemies and rape their relatives, then just made that so much easier. And with all of the unprotected sex, you're going to see a huge spike in STDs.

In short, for most people it's going to be a day of picnics and rainbows, but for others it's going to be a day of blood and murder. There will be a lot of bodies.

2) The Foundation isn't going to be able to hide as many changes as you think. Not all clocks are hooked to the net, and you're ignoring a lot of obvious tells, such as weather patterns and animal movements.

3) You may be ignoring all of those other groups, but with The Foundation dealing with all of those bodies and other issues, this is going to leave them open to attacks on their sites. As such, you need to allow for that.

Straight up: This is an awesome horror event. Not so much a day of peace….

item.title: Pep-Talk Sticky Notes
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article
Elevator Pitch: A sticky note pad that is only useable by personnel currently experiencing negative emotions. When said personnel take one, the message on the note viewable only to them calms them down and leaves them feeling content for a period of three minutes afterward. When the three minutes are up, the subject is left in a neutral state. The messages are reported as upbeat and encouraging.

Central Narrative: It logs how the anomaly is used during testing and ends with a log in which the notepad manifests a secondary anomalous property. It also logs the potential uses of the notepad.

Hook/Attention Grabber I plan the Containment Procedures to be attention-grabbing, with them going something like As SCP-XXXX poses no threat to the security and safety of Site-XX and its personnel, SCP-XXXX is allowed to be freely used whenever it manifests contained in a lock-protected drawer in Dr. XXXXX's office. Also, I plan to put an interview log in which the notepad manifests in the middle of a stressful interview and then manifests to the interviewee after failing the interview miserably.

Additional Notes: I know it's another item SCP, but they work best for my writing style. Also, I want to write this one to be easy to understand for people who have never read an SCP before.

All criticism is appreciated! Thanks!

item.title: Re: Elevator draft, agaiin
item.content:encoded:
It would be good to keep in mind I'm new to the foundation and haven't made an scp yet, so take my criticism with a grain of salt, but these are all the things I noticed while reading it, in the same order as the article.

my (nitpicky) criticism
 my (nitpicky) criticism

I don't get why it would be esoteric? seems like it would be safe, because they can just keep it in one place, no one else has access.

If the O-5 want people to give sightings of Dr. Spencer why would they cover his eyes? I would find a different image if you can't fully show that one.

The forewords are a bit confusing, I didn't immediately know you were talking about the d class, so some disambiguation about that would be good.

Another thing about Test 1 is Dr. Spencer seems oddly unclinical, his words themselves make grammatical sense but it definitely doesn't seem clinical. He should be stating things more factually, instead of words like "hey", "you're welcome", or "lots". It just seems like he should be less replying to the D class, and more telling him what to do in a stricter way.

The diary seems good to me, clinical tone isn't required obviously, but it does seem a bit hamfisted at the end there when he mentions the scp and how he wants to use it all in one sentence at the end.

I thought Test 2 was nice, but it felt a bit forced when you said "Always talked about the 1969 Moon landing". And again, I don't really think a doctor should be saying "hey" during procedure.

The second diary entry seemed better, because it was already established that he wanted to use the elevator, so I don't think a change needs to be present in my opinion.

I like that in the 3rd test, you specify that you're talking about the D-class this time, but I'm not sure why it didn't happen before. The Foreword of this is by far the best of the 3, it doesn't feel especially forced and gives a nice overview of the D class. The test itself seemed fine, but again, Dr. Spencer seems way too non-clinical. Also I don't think there's such a thing as Kauai Beach. Kauai is an Island in Hawaii, but I may be wrong on there being no beach.

Final diary is alright, but I'm confused how he managed to nab 2 pills of scp-500, as those are under super strict lockdown with weight sensors. I also thought the reference to 939 was forced, and there wasn't any mention of him working anywhere near those before.

Overall, the most glaring issues were it being esoteric, the test logs being non-clinical and there were a lot of things that came out of nowhere, like the 939 reference, the moon landing bit, or the sudden diary entry saying he wanted to use the elevator.

Although it might sound like I don't like it, I think this is actually a pretty solid idea, and one that could work really well. As was said in previous thread's criticism, there are other transportation scps, but I can't remember any very similar to this. I would also add a bit more to the description, like if they can interact with the other people there (if any), and if they can, what it looks like to the people in those locations when the elevator comes in (this could be determined by having someone go, finding out their favorite location, sending people to that area, then sending them again).
